issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify getTotalNumberOfStudents() as a no-argument method returning int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests). This is a method-parameter mismatch: students following the specification will implement a no-arg method, while the solution uses a different signature, which can confuse students about the expected API and break comparisons or tests that expect the no-arg method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution match the specification: implement a no-argument getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns the total number of students as described in the UML. If the boolean option to include guests is desired, add an overloaded helper method getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) or implement the boolean variant privately and expose the no-arg public method to preserve the intended API and avoid confusing students.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a no-argument method getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests). This signature difference (extra boolean parameter) breaks the direct mapping between the exercise requirement and the provided implementation: students reading the task expect a no-arg method as specified in the UML/template, while the solution exposes a different API. This creates unnecessary cognitive load and will likely cause confusion or failing tests that expect the no-arg method.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a no-argument method matching the problem/UML: public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns the total number of students (e.g., inscribed + guest). Optionally keep the boolean overload if needed, but ensure the no-arg signature exists so the implementation aligns exactly with the exercise specification and tests.
